contents.text:
I'm settling on the answer: ADR 0027 says the core names no product and splits things into the core engine, identities, and packs, with one composition project. The doc lives at src/docs/adr/0027-engine-identities-and-packs.md. I don't think a ShowPage is needed, since the `/` page already covers this, so I'll offer some options afterward and keep the reply brief.

I'm going to state the status as accepted and dated 2026-10-19, then write the answer in prose, close with the doc path on its own line, and end with the offer.

ADR 0027 decides that the engine names no product. Puls had grown inside `LouisAgent.Core`, so every product built on the engine carried it. The ADR splits the framework into three parts.

The engine, `LouisAgent.Core`, keeps the loop, sessions, usage and prices, guards, the shared contracts, and the tools every identity needs. It names no product and no country.

An identity (`IAgentIdentity`) says who an agent is: its voice, modes, roles, and the packs it uses, by name. Puls, the demo, the coding agent and voorman are all identities.

A pack (`IAgentPack`) says what an agent can do: toolsets, providers, guides, settings, and the packs it requires. A pack never references another pack or an identity.

A single composition project, `src/hosts/LouisAgent.Composition`, knows them all. A host picks its identities and packs with the `IDENTITIES` and `PACKS` settings at start-up.

The result is that a new product is configured rather than coded, and adding one adds no branch to the engine. Identities and packs load only at start-up, so a chat's tools never change while it runs.

Source: `src/docs/adr/0027-engine-identities-and-packs.md`
